help.title: Binomial one-sided lower confidence bound for reliability
help.body:
Binomial One-Sided Lower Confidence Bound for Reliability

Purpose
This analysis computes the one-sided lower confidence bound for reliability when all tested units have passed (i.e., zero failures observed). It is commonly used in reliability demonstration testing to quantify the minimum reliability that can be claimed with a specified confidence level. The method assumes a binomial model where each tested unit results in either success (pass) or failure.
When no failures are observed, the procedure calculates the exact Clopper–Pearson lower confidence bound for the true reliability.

Input data required to perform the analysis

The “Number of samples tested without failure” field should contain the count of tested units that all passed. You may enter a single value or multiple comma-separated values to compute results for several sample sizes simultaneously.
The “Confidence interval” field should contain a value between 0 and 1 (for example, 0.95 for 95% confidence), and multiple comma-separated confidence levels may also be provided.

When multiple values are entered in both fields, calculations are performed pairwise in the order entered.

The output includes the lower bound reliability estimate and the corresponding “Nines” value, which indicates how many consecutive 9s appear in the reliability level (e.g., 0.99 = two nines)

This analysis is appropriate only when zero failures are observed; if failures occur, a different binomial reliability method should be used
